text:
emily chen: Heads-up — we've completed the SLO rebaseline review and are lifting the maintenance weekend freeze. TL;DR: adjusted p99 latency SLO for model-serving routes from 300ms -> 350ms for the next 2 weeks to account for ongoing KV cache warmup after the quantized rollout. This is temporary, targeted, and we've opened an action list to drive improvements.

emily chen: Why we're doing this: last week's load tests exposed sustained p99 variance during cold cache periods on dedicated pools. Rather than trigger pages for expected transient warmup, we prefer to rebalance SLOs and focus on mitigation steps.

emily chen: Timeline: effective immediately (2380012345). Review checkpoint in 2 weeks (2380122345). Maintenance freeze lift: weekend maintenance allowed again starting this Friday 22:00 UTC — please update runbooks before scheduling.

raj singh: ack. can you paste the change to alert thresholds so we can update opsplaybook? :+1:

emily chen: alert delta: routing-service p99 alert threshold 300ms -> 360ms, sustained over 5m. error budget burn action unchanged. I've updated the alerts in cloudwatch and PagerDuty config will be patched during our 30-min maintenance window.

marta velasquez: will we communicate this to affected customers or only internal? worried about enterprise customers with strict SLAs.

emily chen: good call. customer comms: for enterprise contracts with hard SLAs we will NOT change their effective SLA. This rebaseline applies to default hosted tier only. CS is drafting a short note for enterprise accounts; @kevin ho will coordinate.

kevin ho: on it — drafting now and will share in #customer-success by EOD. also can we get a one-liner for external comms? short and non-technical.

oncall-bot: Incident ticket created: INC-2026-3017 "p99 variance during cold KV cache after quantized rollout" — assigned to emily chen. Link: https://incidents.example/INC-2026-3017

marta velasquez: thanks. any immediate mitigation I should run if alerts spike over weekend?

emily chen: mitigation steps in runbook link below. short form: 1) scale dedicated pools by +10% (k8s label: workload=dedicated-serving) 2) enable kvcache-prefetch on affected prefixes 3) temporarily route users to warmed variants via routing policy. Command snippets:

echo "scale" && kubectl -n inference scale deployment/dedicated-pool --replicas=$(($(kubectl get deploy dedicated-pool -o jsonpath='{.status.replicas}')+2))

emily chen: Runbook: https://runbooks.internal/sre/slo-rebaseline-and-kv-warmup

ops-runbook-bot: Runbook last-updated by emily chen at 2380012400 — changes: added preflight checks and alert updates.

raj singh: one more ask — let's gate any risky maintenance (kernel/drivers) on canary success and a quick sled test. prefer manual approval for first 24h after lifting freeze.

emily chen: agreed. added a guardrail: any kernel/driver maintenance requires a canary runbook sign-off and @emily chen + @raj singh approval. See runbook section "Canary Gate"

kevin ho: pushed customer draft to #customer-success. feedback welcome.

marta velasquez: thanks everyone. I'll update the SLO doc and add a note for platform teams. :heavy_check_mark:

emily chen: thanks team. ping me directly if you need help executing mitigations this weekend. :rocket:
